div.p: A Splunk alert creates an incident or a risk in Adversarial. The app adds one alert action for each record type:

ul.li: Create Adversarial incident for an event. Something happened, and somebody must respond.
Create Adversarial risk for a standing condition. Something is weak, and somebody must remediate it.

div.p: Both actions use the same credential service account. To create one, open the Adversarial platform, go to Settings > Team > Service Accounts, and click Create. Give it the roles that it needs: Incident Editor to create incidents, Risk Editor to create risks, or both roles to use both actions. The Editor role holds both. Copy the client ID and the client secret before you close the dialog.

div.label: API URL
div.span: The base URL of the API. Keep the /api path element.

div.label: Client secret
div.span: Splunk keeps the secret encrypted. The page never shows it again.

ol.li: Create an alert, or open an existing one.
Under Trigger Actions, add Create Adversarial incident or Create Adversarial risk. One alert can hold both actions.
Set the title and the source, then save the alert. Leave the score fields empty to let AI Suggest Score assign the incident severity, or the risk urgency.

div.p: The source must be one of the sources of your organization. The two record types hold two separate lists: Settings > Incidents and Settings > Risks in the Adversarial platform.
To test the connection from a search, run one of these commands:

pre.code:
| makeresults | sendalert adversarial_incident param.title="Test incident from Splunk" param.source="SIEM"
| makeresults | sendalert adversarial_risk param.title="Test risk from Splunk" param.source="Attack Surface Monitoring"

div.p: Change the source names to the sources of your organization. The app holds one example alert for each action, both disabled after an install. Find them in Settings > Searches, reports, and alerts.
